1 Purpose and analytical position

This report finalises a site-first interpretation of the Holtemme WGCNA network. It does not reconstruct the network and does not use chemistry to select modules. Instead, it follows five ordered questions:

  1. Which module eigengenes differ among the six sampling sites or across the three predefined river transitions?
  2. Which modules retain acceptable membership and eigengene-profile stability across a declared 14-network sensitivity scheme?
  3. Which biological functions are enriched in the complete gene membership of those modules, using the selected WGCNA gene universe as the functional background?
  4. Which differentially expressed genes and highly connected genes provide gene-level support for the module interpretation?
  5. Do total predicted mixture pressure or selected mode-of-action (MoA) profiles provide compatible chemical context for the independently selected modules?

The network was constructed from 30 individual RNA-seq libraries. Site effects and planned module-eigengene contrasts are therefore evaluated from individual library values. Chemistry remains measured once per site; chemistry overlays use six site means and are treated as secondary, hypothesis-generating context.

Module eigengene signs are mathematically arbitrary. A positive site contrast means that the module eigengene had a higher value at the numerator site; it does not by itself mean that every gene in the module was upregulated. Gene-level expression direction is evaluated separately using the focal differential- expression contrasts.

The valid non-grey modules multiplied by the three predefined contrasts form the sole primary inferential family. Omnibus site tests are supplementary, and chemistry never selects modules.

4 2. Network-design transparency and input quality control

This section records what the existing network represents. It does not treat the scale-free-topology statistic as a measure of network accuracy. 5 3. Module stability under resampling and parameter variation

Module membership stability is evaluated before modules are interpreted. The declared scheme contains 14 alternative networks: ten site-stratified subsamples retaining four of five libraries per site, two full-data soft-power variants at plus/minus two from the selected power, and two full-data merge-height variants (0.15 and 0.35). Each reference module is matched to the alternative module with the greatest gene-membership Jaccard index. Absolute eigengene-profile agreement is evaluated after projecting each alternative assignment onto all 30 libraries.

The diagnostic is descriptive rather than a preservation significance test. high and moderate modules pass the stability gate; low modules can be shown as exploratory patterns but cannot support a paper-facing module claim. Cached results are reused only when the source files, WGCNA version, random seed, and declared settings have an identical fingerprint.

6 4. Primary site association of module eigengenes

The three planned contrasts are the sole primary WGCNA test family. Benjamini-Hochberg correction is applied once across the dynamically determined family of valid non-grey modules multiplied by three contrasts. The omnibus site tests are a supplementary overview and cannot independently select a module. Adjustment within each contrast is also exported as a diagnostic, not as a second inferential route.

Because the modules were derived from these same 30 expression profiles, these p-values are exploratory measures of site structure rather than validation in an independent dataset.

6.1 Contrast-level robustness of the retained modules

Module membership stability does not by itself demonstrate that a focal site contrast is insensitive to individual organisms. The three FDR-supported, stability-gated modules are therefore evaluated through leave-one-individual-out refitting, site-stratified bootstrap resampling, and exact two-group permutation. These are sensitivity diagnostics; the globally adjusted planned contrast remains the primary inferential test.

Contrast sensitivity of the three FDR-supported, stability-gated modules. Exact permutation p-values are descriptive and do not replace the globally adjusted planned tests.

7 5. Differential-expression overlap in the focal contrasts

8 6. Whole-module GO enrichment

The functional target is the complete gene membership of each assigned module. The background is the same selected gene universe that was eligible to enter the WGCNA network. This avoids comparing a variance-selected module against the much larger expression-filtered transcriptome.

The primary analysis uses the EggNOG-derived gene-to-GO mapping already prepared in Step 04. GOseq is used with median gene-level transcript length as a bias proxy. Module-level FDR is calculated within each complete module enrichment, while a global FDR across all module-term tests is exported as a conservative sensitivity column. The broader Trinotate union is processed identically as a declared sensitivity analysis. GO identifiers are audited against the current local GO.db before either analysis; obsolete or unknown identifiers are retained in an audit table but excluded when no explicit local replacement is available.

8.1 Ontology-specific Wang semantic reduction

RRvGO-style reduction is applied only after GOseq significance testing. BP, MF, and CC are reduced separately using Wang similarity from the current GO graph. The similarity calculation is topology based and therefore does not import annotation frequencies from an unrelated organism OrgDb. The clustering and representative-term structure follows RRvGO: terms are hierarchically clustered from their semantic-similarity matrix and the term with the largest -log10(module-wide FDR) score represents each cluster. This step reduces redundancy; it is not a new significance test or module-selection route.

9 7. Site-first module selection and detailed functional dossiers

The primary paper-facing gate requires both a globally FDR-supported planned contrast and acceptable module stability. Whole-module functional enrichment, DEG overlap, and interpretable hubs determine whether a gate-passing module has enough biological content for detailed interpretation. When a contrast has no FDR-supported module, its two leading absolute effects remain visible as an explicitly exploratory ranking; neither the omnibus tests nor chemistry can promote those modules into the primary family.

Site-first modules retained for detailed functional inspection; effect-size ranking uses the six-site model-standardized contrast.

9.1 Supportive whole-module KEGG enrichment

KEGG pathways are tested as a separate supportive family using the EggNOG gene-to-pathway mapping prepared in Step 04, the same selected WGCNA background, and the same length-bias correction. KEGG does not determine module selection and is not subjected to GO semantic reduction. Local pathway identifiers are retained verbatim where no versioned local pathway-name catalogue is available.

10 8. Hub genes, DEG support, and enriched-term traceback

Hub status describes strong membership in the module’s dominant expression profile. It does not show that a hub gene responds directly to a chemical or MoA. The gene dossier therefore keeps module connectivity, focal DEG support, and whole-module functional traceback as separate evidence columns.

11 9. Chemistry overlay after site and function selection

Total predicted mixture pressure is retained as the primary quantitative chemistry context. The five direct MoA-specific summed-TU profiles are secondary exploratory descriptors. They do not determine which modules enter the site-first functional dossiers.

13 11. Final paper-facing WGCNA figure

The final figure is restricted to modules that pass the global planned-contrast FDR, the declared membership-stability gate, and the contrast-level robustness check. The green module is required. The turquoise module is included only when its H3–H2 contrast retains direction in every focal leave-one-out refit and in at least 95% of site-stratified bootstrap samples. The magenta module is reported separately because its sparse annotation does not support pathway-level interpretation.

Figure legend. Site-associated co-expression modules retained after the predefined site-contrast, module-stability, and contrast-sensitivity gates. (A) Individual-library module eigengene values across the six sampling sites; diamonds and error bars show site means and 95% confidence intervals. Dotted vertical lines mark the H2–H3 and H5–H6 transitions. (B) Planned contrast estimates. Thin intervals are model-based 95% confidence intervals, while thick pale intervals are site-stratified bootstrap 95% intervals. Labels report global BH-adjusted q-values and the proportions of leave-one-out and bootstrap estimates retaining the fitted direction. (C) Contrast-specific DEGs and the remaining genes in each complete module. (D) Specific, traceable whole-module functional families assigned from primary-mapping FDR GO terms after excluding generic parent terms. Module eigengene signs are arbitrary. Differential- expression and co-expression analyses summarize the same libraries and provide complementary rather than independent evidence.

13.1 Supplementary magenta-module profile

14 12. Exploratory interpretation

14.1 Analytical outcome

The site-first screen evaluated 18 assigned modules across 30 individual libraries. 5 modules met FDR < 0.05 in the supplementary omnibus overview. 4 of the 54 primary planned module-contrast tests met global FDR < 0.05; 3 distinct modules also passed the formal membership-stability gate, and 2 passed the additional contrast-level robustness rule for main-text display. 15 planned tests combined nominal p < 0.05 with an absolute model-standardized effect >= 1.00. Pairwise Hedges’ g is retained only as an archival diagnostic and does not rank modules.

Whole-module enrichment identified at least one module-level FDR GO term in 4 assigned modules. Ontology-specific Wang reduction produced representative term clusters for 4 modules, while the separate supportive KEGG family identified at least one FDR pathway in 4 modules. These results describe the functional composition of complete modules rather than only the subsets already recovered through differential expression.

The primary EggNOG GO mapping retained annotations for 994 of the 10,000 network genes. The broader Trinotate-union sensitivity mapping retained 1755 genes and is reported only as a robustness comparison. The current GO.db audit flagged 0 obsolete or unresolved identifiers. Paper-facing functional families exclude generic GO parents and remain traceable to their source terms and module genes.

14.2 Modules by focal transition

** First WWTP transition H3 vs H2 .** MEturquoise (difference = -0.327, model-standardized effect = -2.00, global q = 0.044; stability = high; paper role = main_text_primary; leading whole-module theme: Other or unresolved function); MEblack (difference = -0.284, model-standardized effect = -1.79, global q = 0.067; stability = low; leading whole-module theme: not resolved).

** Second WWTP transition H6 vs H5 .** MEgreen (difference = -0.324, model-standardized effect = -2.33, global q = 0.044; stability = moderate; paper role = main_text_primary; leading whole-module theme: Other or unresolved function); MEmagenta (difference = 0.250, model-standardized effect = 2.03, global q = 0.044; stability = moderate; paper role = supplementary_stable_sparse_annotation; leading whole-module theme: not resolved).

** Furthest downstream site H7 vs H2 .** MEred (difference = 0.327, model-standardized effect = 2.07, global q = 0.044; stability = low; leading whole-module theme: Other or unresolved function); MEgreen (difference = 0.257, model-standardized effect = 1.85, global q = 0.064; stability = moderate; leading whole-module theme: Other or unresolved function).

14.3 Interpretation boundary

Only modules supported in the globally adjusted 54-test planned-contrast family and passing the declared membership-stability gate are eligible for a primary module-level claim. Main-text display additionally requires a contrast direction that survives every focal leave-one-out refit and at least 95% of site-stratified bootstrap samples. Whole-module enrichment, focal DEG overlap, and interpretable high-kME genes strengthen biological interpretation but are complementary summaries of the same transcriptomic dataset, not independent replication. Chemistry and MoA profiles are applied only after biological selection and cannot establish chemical causation.
